clauses.evidence: [stimulus: this creature attacks alone, unblocked]: DECLARE_ATTACKERS with no 'card becomes tapped' event

clauses.clause: When this creature enters, you may search your library and/or graveyard for a card named Garruk, Savage Herald, ... and put it into your hand.
clauses.evidence: trace: the ETB triggers (also on the opponent's turn) with 'ask may: [fire, skip]'; the standard board has no Garruk, so nothing is found either way. Tree: OptionalEffect(Seq(SEARCH ONE_OF NAME_EQ 'Garruk, Savage Herald' in GRAVEYARD(YOU)+LIBRARY(YOU) -> HAND(YOU), REVEAL, SHUFFLE)). Packs PASS on this packet's tree (run as a draft) and on the live tree: K_garruks_warsteed_finds_garruk_in_library.json (found in your library -> hand; a differently named card stays), K_garruks_warsteed_finds_garruk_in_graveyard.json (found in your graveyard -> hand; the opponent's copy in their graveyard is never taken), K_garruks_warsteed_declined_search.json ('skip' leaves Garruk in the library).
clauses.issue: minor, weaker only: the compiler's sentence tree (`similar` B2b-named-card-search) uses mode=CHOOSE, this tree ONE_OF, so after choosing to search the player cannot fail to find (CR 701.23b allows it in the library). No strength gain.

clauses.evidence: a debug replay of the library pack shows the row ('REVEAL', 'player:0', ('card:10',)): the top card of the library, not the found Garruk (card:1).
clauses.issue: engine quirk (not stronger or weaker in play): REVEAL is a recorded no-op with the top-N-of-library convention (verbs.py _look), so 'reveal it' records the library's top card instead of the searched card; the per-seat view does not track revealed cards at all (bench/view.py module note), so no seat gains or loses information. Same REVEAL atom in the canonical compile of every 'search for a card named X, reveal it' card (Teferi's Wavecaster, Goldmane Griffin).

clauses.clause: If you search your library this way, shuffle.
clauses.evidence: no pack lane can assert a shuffle; debug replay of the packs on this packet's tree: after 'fire' a ('SHUFFLE', 'player:0', 'library') row follows the search and the library order changes; after 'skip' no shuffle and the order is unchanged. Every 'fire' searches the library, so shuffling then is right.
